language_wrapper: On a {rows}x{cols} grid table, a white piece and a black piece are randomly and independently placed in different cells with equal probability over ordered pairs. Alice (white) moves first. Each move must be exactly one cell horizontally or vertically, and for the same piece, horizontal and vertical moves must alternate. In this variant, the first move of the white piece must be {white_first}, and the first move of the black piece must be {black_first}; thereafter, each piece continues alternating between horizontal and vertical moves. Bob wins if after one of his moves the two pieces occupy exactly the same cell; if Bob can prevent this from ever happening, Alice wins. Let p = m/n be the probability (in lowest terms) that Bob has a winning strategy, where the probability is taken over all ordered initial placements of the two pieces in different cells. Find m.
hardness_rationale: The family upgrades the seed by simultaneously (i) allowing a general rectangular board and (ii) fixing the forced first-move orientations for each player. This eliminates the simplifying symmetry in the seed (where players could choose their initial orientation), creating an inherently asymmetric, turn-based reachability game. The correct solution requires modeling the game as a finite alternating graph and computing the attractor of Bob’s capture set via retrograde analysis (fixed-point iteration over predecessors), rather than relying on parity/coloring heuristics alone. This graph-theoretic game approach is more advanced and less guessable, and the outcome depends in a subtle way on the board’s aspect ratio and the two starting orientations.
notes: Implementation uses standard reachability game (attractor) computation on a finite turn-based graph of size O((rc)^2) with constant out-degree. For maintainers: the alternation constraints are encoded in the state by tracking each piece’s next-axis bit. Immediate-capture edges (Bob moving onto White) are treated as transitions to a terminal winning sink; the algorithm seeds the attractor with all such Bob-turn states and propagates wins backward. Initial placements are ordered pairs of distinct cells to match the uniform random process described.
source_question: On a \(2025\times2025\) grid table, one white piece and one black piece are randomly placed in different cells. Alice moves the white piece first, then Bob moves the black piece, and they move alternately, and the following rules are satisfied: Each move can only be one cell horizontally or vertically, and for the same piece, horizontal and vertical moves must be alternated. If after Bob's move, the black piece and the white piece exactly fall into the same cell, then Bob wins; otherwise, Alice wins. Let \(p = m/n\) be the probability that Bob has a winning strategy where \(m\) and \(n\) are coprime. Find \(m\).
